children: According to ChainCatcher citing PC Gamer and CoinGecko, a leaker who identifies as Cyberleek distributed a torrent of what they claim is a near-complete 209 GB Xbox version of GTA 6 from November 2026, but withheld the game’s main executable. Modders would need the file to simulate the game on PC, potentially enabling an unofficial PC version before Rockstar Games’ planned release.

Cyberleek said the executable will be released on November 23 regardless of the token’s price, but could be published earlier if the CYBERLEEK token reaches a $15 million market capitalization. That target is half the $30 million goal the leaker set in October. CoinGecko data put the token at about $0.002 and a market capitalization of roughly $1.3 million over the weekend, more than $13 million short of the threshold and down about 20% over the past week. The low-cap token has thin liquidity and volatile prices.

None of the leaked files has been independently verified as genuine, and GTA 6 has no officially announced PC version. Rockstar, which is known for pursuing legal action, could respond with litigation rather than a port. The article also notes that Xbox games’ architecture is closer to PC software than PlayStation games, while AI coding tools have accelerated reverse engineering and contributed to a wave of AI-assisted game ports this year.

title: GTA 6 Leaker Withholds Executable, Sets $15M Token Market Cap Threshold
